summary: The prepared base already contains upstream PR #37441, which admits an explicitly requested backend by platform and capability even when it is absent from a model's automatic-selection set. An issue-specific FLUX.2 regression passes on the base and fails with the exact reported whitelist error when the pre-#37441 membership check is restored.

tests.what_was_measured: Three FLUX.2-specific selector cases passed: explicit SAGE_ATTN bypasses the model automatic-selection set, implicit selection still respects it, and missing backend capabilities still fail closed.

tests.command: pre-#37441 selector membership check + pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_attention_backend_selector.py -k flux2_explicit_sage_backend_bypasses
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: the same regression raised the reported ValueError because FLUX.2's set excludes sage_attn. The prepared-base selector was restored immediately afterward.
Complete selector unit suite: 28 tests and 4 subtests passed.
The assigned GPU was identified as AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, and the real ROCm resolver rejected SAGE_ATTN as unsupported on ROCm.

gpu_execution_evidence: The assigned single GPU is AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, but SGLang's ROCm platform resolver raises 'SAGE_ATTN is not supported on rocm.' No relevant SageAttention GPU kernel was executed.
remaining_limitations: No CUDA Blackwell GPU was available, so the SageAttention CUDA resolver and kernel were not executed.
FLUX.2-klein-9b-kv weights were not available, so full model construction, serving startup, image generation, and semantic accuracy were not tested.
The regression validates the selector/model-whitelist boundary with a deterministic fake platform backend; it does not validate SageAttention numerical output.
